A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DIA and have readable text, equations, tables and figures. However, v1 includes three supplementary pages, whereas v2 ends with references despite referring to supplementary material. Comparisons of appendix-only proofs, implementation details and experiments are therefore limited.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component and similarity-metric ablations, feature visualizations, and supplementary hyperparameter and architecture experiments.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, feature-reconstruction comparisons and additional distillation-control experiments.

M1.justification: v1's PDL equation applies a stop-gradient operator to the angular weight; v2's Eq. 14 omits this operator and its explanation, changing the specified gradient handling. Implementation intent is unexplained. TSAI routing and PFR mixing otherwise remain equivalent; the two-stage optimization description largely restates v1's supplement.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-21K pretraining and evaluate CIFAR-100, CUB-200, ImageNet-R and ImageNet-A. The ten-task evaluations and twenty-task ImageNet-R/CIFAR-100 evaluations already appear in v1. No additional dataset or task coverage is established.

E2.justification: v2 adds C-ADA and InfLoRA to Table 1 and InfLoRA to the twenty-task comparison, renumbered from Table 3 to Table 2. Table 5 adds all-token L1 distillation and PDL including the class token. v1's supplementary CLIP-MoE comparison is unavailable in the supplied v2.

E3.justification: The stated initial learning rate changes from 0.025 to 0.015. Figure 3's visualization changes from the first ten classes to the first twenty. The backbone, twenty training epochs, batch size 32, class orders and principal incremental-task protocols remain unchanged. These statements do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds tests of all-token distillation and inclusion of the class token, while Figure 3 adds localized decision-boundary analysis. The beta and lambda sweeps in v2's Figure 4 already existed in v1's supplement. Changes to the earlier margin, adapter-rank and placement studies cannot be checked without v2's supplement.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seed variation, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional results retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises DIA's ImageNet-A final/average accuracy from 59.78/70.43 to 61.69/71.58 and CUB-200 average accuracy from 92.13 to 93.21. Table 4 changes DIA-Gau's ImageNet-R final accuracy from 78.08 to 76.07; Table 5 changes cosine-weighted PDL's average from 84.76 to 85.16. New comparator/control results also appear. The changed learning rate prevents treating these as controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The main-text SVD and task-subspace derivation is retained with equivalent notation. v1's supplement supplies the explicit nonlinear/ReLU derivation, while v2 refers to supplementary analysis that is not included. Whether that derivation was retained, corrected or removed cannot be established.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain DIA, patch-level adapter integration, PDL and PFR. Both versions claim state-of-the-art performance across four benchmarks and up to approximately 90% lower inference computation. Updated supporting results do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning PDL's stability–plasticity trade-off, excessive regularization at larger lambda, and inaccurate alignment at small beta. It expands discussion of reconstructed decision boundaries and omits v1's explanation that negative cosine weights cause loss cancellation.

D1.justification: v2 revises the documented learning rate and removes v1's future code-release promise. Its lambda value and sampling of 32 prototypes were already disclosed in v1's supplement, so their main-text appearance is relocation. The full training algorithm and cosine-margin details cannot be compared because v2's referenced supplement is unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 expands discussion of drift compensation and continual adapters, adds citations including LDC, C-ADA, InfLoRA and the ADAM source paper, and removes the EMA reference. The overall positioning within parameter-efficient, non-exemplar incremental learning remains intact.

P1.justification: The paper receives numerous local language refinements, numbered sections, updated author information and acknowledgments. An Optimization Objective subsection brings existing supplementary material into the main text, and the long-sequence and component analyses are reordered. The principal narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn, and Figure 3 becomes a substantially expanded three-panel visualization with decision regions and enlarged error examples. Existing supplementary beta/lambda plots are combined into main-text Figure 4. Tables are expanded, regrouped and relocated, alongside extensive changes to typography and layout.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the visible comparisons and distillation analyses and improves explanatory figures. However, its missing referenced supplement prevents assessing important proofs, training details and structural ablations. Reporting consistency also worsens: Table 1 implies a 2.70-point CUB-200 advantage over EASE, while the text retains 1.62. These benefits, documentation gaps and reporting problems prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
